question: A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pain and weakness in her right forearm and hand for several months. Two years ago, she sustained a fracture of her ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head that was treated surgically. Physical examination shows mild tenderness a few centimeters distal to the lateral epicondyle. She has marked weakness when attempting to extend her right middle finger. There is radial deviation on extension of the wrist. Sensation is not impaired. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "25-year-old woman with forearm pain" -> "history of ulnar shaft fracture and radial head dislocation" -> "tenderness distal to lateral epicondyle" -> "marked weakness in extending right middle finger" -> "radial deviation on wrist extension" -> "indicates possible radial nerve involvement" -> "posterior interosseous nerve is a branch of the radial nerve" -> "likely affected due to history and symptoms" -> 85%

CHAIN: "25-year-old woman with forearm pain" -> "sustained fracture and dislocation two years ago" -> "tenderness near lateral epicondyle" -> "weakness in finger extension" -> "radial deviation suggests wrist extensor weakness" -> "posterior interosseous nerve innervates wrist extensors" -> "most likely affected nerve" -> 90%

CHAIN: "25-year-old woman with pain and weakness" -> "previous ulnar shaft fracture" -> "tenderness near lateral epicondyle" -> "weakness in extending middle finger" -> "radial deviation on wrist extension" -> "suggests radial nerve dysfunction" -> "posterior interosseous nerve affected" -> 80%

CHAIN: "25-year-old woman with right forearm pain" -> "history of surgical treatment for fracture" -> "tenderness distal to lateral epicondyle" -> "weakness in finger extension" -> "radial deviation indicates extensor weakness" -> "posterior interosseous nerve likely affected" -> "confident due to symptom correlation" -> 90%
analysis: The symptoms described, including pain and weakness in the right forearm and hand, marked weakness in extending the middle finger, and radial deviation on wrist extension, suggest an issue with the radial nerve. Specifically, the posterior interosseous nerve, a branch of the radial nerve, innervates the extensor muscles of the forearm, including those responsible for extending the fingers. The history of a previous ulnar shaft fracture and radial head dislocation may have contributed to nerve injury or entrapment. Therefore, the most likely affected nerve in this patient is the posterior interosseous nerve.
